test_run_counting_note: Counted from this session's own transcript: distinct tool invocations whose output contained a unittest or pytest result line. Includes targeted single-module runs as well as full-suite runs.
final_test_command: python -m pytest -q  (equivalently: PYTHONPATH=src:tests python -m unittest discover -s tests -q)
major_modelling_decisions: Schedule convention inferred from the data rather than assumed: schedules run backwards from maturity with n = max(1, round(T x frequency)) periods and accrual 1/frequency. Tested against the quotes -- ceil misprices the 1.25Y annual OIS by ~50bp and floor misprices the 2.44Y semiannual bond by ~60bp; round is the only rule consistent with every instrument in the file. CONVENTIONS.md is silent on this point.

Both estimators are parameterised through the instantaneous forward rate, so D(T) = exp(-integral f) is strictly positive by construction and negative rates need no special case. Verified end to end on a wholly negative synthetic data set.
Baseline: sequential bootstrap of consensus pillars with log-linear discount factors (piecewise-constant instantaneous forwards); pillars closer than 0.10Y merged. It reprices every pillar exactly.

Advanced (published): cubic spline in the instantaneous forward, objective sum(w_i rho(r_i)) + lambda * integral (T/1Y)^p f''(T)^2 dT, with residuals in yield-equivalent basis points (bond price residuals converted by -1e4/(P*Duration)) and rho the Tukey biweight. lambda and the maturity exponent p are selected by maturity-blocked cross-validation on training data only (selected lambda=1e-5, p=2, 21 knots snapped to the benchmark rate maturities).
The roughness penalty is maturity-weighted. An unweighted penalty over-smooths the money-market end, which is where the term structure genuinely bends most.

Weights: sigma_i^2 = sigma_quote,i^2 + sigma_model,type^2. The second term is estimated from a preliminary robust fit's residual MAD per instrument type (bond 2.14bp, ois_swap 0.56bp, deposit floored at 0.25bp). Bid/ask alone implies sigma ~ 0.1bp for instruments that genuinely disagree by 2-3bp, so a spread-only weighting scheme would be badly overconfident about the bonds.

Robustness: convex Huber warm-up (c=1.345, 4 sweeps) before Tukey-biweight IRLS (c=4.685), with the robust scale re-estimated for three sweeps and then frozen. Started cold, the redescending estimator converged onto the contaminated cluster of quotes on this data and rejected the good majority.

Outlier exclusion requires two conditions: more than 4.685 robust sigma from a deliberately flexible robust reference fit AND at least 5bp (yield-equivalent) from the observation's own maturity neighbours. Residuals are measured locally (a shorth of the same-pillar residuals, or the median of the 8 nearest maturities) so that a whole pillar cannot be deleted, and at most 25% of the sample can be removed.

Holdout is maturity-blocked, never random: a new block starts when the maturity gap exceeds max(0.15Y, 2% of T), every 4th interior block is withheld, and first and last blocks are never withheld. The file has four venues quoting the same 10Y pillar and bonds maturing days apart from benchmark swaps, so a random split would leave a near-identical instrument in training and measure quote dispersion instead of curve quality. A test demonstrates the blocked holdout error is more than 3x a random split's on deliberately duplicated data.

Selection rule, fixed before any number was inspected: (1) reject any curve whose instantaneous forward leaves the quoted rate range by more than 200bp; (2) among admissible curves take the lower maturity-blocked holdout weighted RMSE, requiring the advanced estimator to beat the baseline by a 5% parsimony margin. On this data the gate is decisive and overturns the accuracy ranking: the bootstrap wins on the holdout (0.71bp vs 1.15bp) but its instantaneous forward runs from -1.76% to +5.85% against a quoted range of 1.21%-2.58%, which makes forward-starting valuation and key-rate risk unusable. Both models' diagnostics are published so the trade-off can be re-made.

Risk: DV01 = (PV[-1bp] - PV[+1bp])/2 under a parallel zero-rate bump, receiver-fixed, notional 1,000,000 for deposits and swaps and face 100 for bonds. Key rates use triangular tent bumps at 2/5/10/30Y that sum to 1 at every maturity, so the buckets add back to the parallel DV01 (5.3e-7 relative). Every finite difference is cross-checked against an analytic cash-flow derivative (1.3e-6 relative).

Publication grid is geometric below 2Y and uniform above it. A uniform 601-point grid leaves 0.55bp of linear-interpolation error inside the first six months -- larger than every money-market repricing residual in the file, and purely an artefact of publication. On the grid actually published that error is below 0.01bp everywhere.

Determinism is a design constraint, not an accident: no RNG anywhere, sorted outputs, %.12g float formatting, sort_keys JSON, PNG Software metadata stripped, and the report stamped with the market snapshot rather than the wall clock. Two independent runs (different virtual environments, different output directories) produced byte-identical CSV, JSON, PNG and HTML.
self_identified_weaknesses: FIXED - Knot budget was driven only by sample size (one knot per four observations), so a small but wide data set got a basis too coarse to bend at the front: a 16-instrument training split spanning 1M-30Y received four knots and mis-priced the 1M deposit by 10.5bp. Added a maturity-coverage floor of four knots per log-decade; the effective degrees of freedom are controlled by the cross-validated penalty, not by the knot count.

FIXED - Cross-validation was skipped whenever the basis was generous relative to the sample (len(instruments) < 2 * n_knots), silently falling back to an arbitrary median lambda. That is backwards for a penalised spline, where choosing lambda is exactly what matters when the basis is generous. The gate is now on sample size.

FIXED - The outlier screen's robust scale collapsed. With a flexible reference fit the scale fell to a fraction of a basis point, and quotes sitting 2bp from their neighbours -- inside any plausible bid/ask -- registered as 40-sigma outliers. Raised the scale floor to 0.5bp and added an absolute 5bp economic gate; on the benchmark data three legitimate bond quotes (4.4-5.1bp yield-equivalent, against a measured 2.14bp bond idiosyncratic spread) were reinstated with low weight instead of deleted.

FIXED - The published curve grid was uniform in maturity, so a consumer linearly interpolating zero_rate between rows picked up 0.55bp of error inside the first six months. Replaced with a geometric front segment; the error is now under 0.01bp everywhere.

FIXED - The HTML report stamped the wall-clock generation time, which broke byte-level reproducibility of the deliverable. It now carries the market snapshot timestamp, which is both deterministic and more informative.
FIXED - Chart PNGs relied on matplotlib's default metadata. Software metadata is now stripped explicitly so charts are byte-identical across matplotlib versions.

FIXED - np.nanmedian was called on a possibly all-NaN slice in the wide-spread check, emitting a RuntimeWarning on degenerate input. It now requires at least one finite bid/ask width. The test suite promotes RuntimeWarning and FutureWarning to errors so this class of defect cannot pass silently again.

FIXED - The report's executive summary quoted the deposit weighted RMSE while describing it as the 'deposit and OIS' figure. It now reports all three instrument types with their sample sizes and says explicitly that the bond figure is the bonds' own idiosyncratic spread rather than a curve error.
FIXED - The report claimed every convention came from the supplied CONVENTIONS.md when the period-count rule for non-integer maturities was in fact inferred from the quotes. Corrected to say so.

FIXED - The cleaning audit table in the report rendered its most valuable column (the reason for each decision) off the right edge of a horizontal scroller, where nobody would read it. Free-text columns now wrap in place.

FIXED (earlier in the run) - The analytic cross-check of DV01 disagreed with the finite difference by a relative 1.96 on OIS swaps: a sign error in the floating-leg derivative. This is exactly what the verification requirement exists for; agreement is now 1.3e-6.

FIXED (earlier in the run) - The outlier screen, driven by whole-sample residuals against a cross-validated fit, deleted entire pillars (four 2.5Y swaps, three 7Y swaps) because the smoother's bias at a genuine term-structure feature looked like a cluster of bad quotes. Replaced with a fixed flexible reference fit, pillar-local residuals, and a neighbourhood-preservation guard.

FIXED (earlier in the run) - Unit-scale detection missed a genuinely mis-scaled short deposit on a steep curve because the peer-comparison threshold was too strict. Replaced with a two-condition rule (four times closer to the peer level AND within 35% of it); all seven genuine cases in the file are caught and no clean synthetic quote is touched.

OPEN - Single-curve assumption. Deposits, OIS swaps and bonds are discounted on one curve; the bond basis is absorbed into an estimated per-type error rather than modelled. This is the largest modelling assumption in the project and is stated rather than hidden.

OPEN - No out-of-time validation. Every stability claim is cross-sectional, because the file is one snapshot. Day-to-day stability -- the property that actually matters for a hedging book -- is untested.

OPEN - Estimated per-type model error is computed from a preliminary fit that itself uses weights, so there is a single-pass circularity. It is deliberately not iterated to convergence, and the outlier-exclusion sensitivity check (1.95bp) measures how much it matters here.
unresolved_limitations: Single discount curve for deposits, OIS swaps and coupon bonds; no funding or credit basis is modelled, so cross-product (bond versus swap) relative value must not use this curve without an asset-swap spread.
No out-of-time validation: one market snapshot, so day-to-day stability of the curve and of the key-rate ladder is unmeasured. This is the most important gap.
No independent benchmark curve to compare against; 'correct' means internally consistent and consistent with the quotes.
The 200bp forward-admissibility tolerance and the 5% parsimony margin are judgements fixed in advance and published, but not themselves validated. They are decisive on this data set.
Convention inference (the period count for non-integer maturities) is validated only against this file; a source built on a different convention would be silently mis-priced.
Below 1/12Y and beyond 30Y the instantaneous forward is held flat. That is a stated policy, not information; no instrument constrains either region.
The 20Y-30Y region contains almost no instruments, so its shape is penalty-driven. The leave-one-block-out check (5.63bp) is the honest uncertainty there, not the 0.9bp repricing RMSE.
The curve is C2 in the forward and therefore cannot represent a genuine kink (a turn-of-year or meeting-date effect); such a feature would be smeared across neighbouring maturities.
The estimator has only ever been shown smooth (Nelson-Siegel) synthetic shapes, so its behaviour on an inverted or discontinuous curve is untested.
No uncertainty band is published: curves/curve.csv carries point estimates, and the sensitivity suite brackets them rather than giving a posterior.
Bond accrued interest is assumed zero because prices are quoted clean and no settlement convention beyond settlement_days is supplied.
The outlier screen is purely cross-sectional; with one snapshot it cannot detect a uniformly wrong pillar, and it is capped at removing 25% of the sample.
integrity_statement: All work was performed inside the dedicated output directory. Only the benchmark input directory, files created in the output directory, and standard system/runtime files were read. No parent, sibling, or other candidate directory was inspected, no previous benchmark run, branch, worktree, shell history or evaluator/hidden-test material was accessed, no supplied benchmark data was altered and no replacement data was created, and no other model or external AI service was used to solve or review the task. Two project-local virtual environments were created inside the output directory for development and for verifying the documented installation instructions; both were removed before completion, and neither reused any other run's environment or caches. This session's own transcript was read once, at the end, solely to recover the recorded start timestamp and to count test-suite invocations for this file.
